# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 30 (Bu-Vb Pc30)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc30  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 30  
**Title (English, from literature):** Sitting alone with a nun  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rahonisajja Sikkhāpada* constitutes the thirtieth *pācittiya* training rule of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka. The core rule formulated in the Pātimokkha stipulates an offense of expiation for any monk who sits down in private, one-on-one, with a Buddhist nun (*yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā saddhiṁ eko ekāya raho nisajjaṁ kappeyya pācittiyaṁ*) [Dutt 1924]. According to the rule's non-offense clause (*anāpatti*), it is not considered an infraction if the monk remains standing rather than sitting down, a distinction shared with related regulations such as Pācittiya 44 and 45 and corroborated by the casuistry of Aniyata 1 and 2 [Hüsken 1997]. In the commentary tradition, Buddhaghosa's *Samantapāsādikā* does not provide an independent exposition for Pācittiya 30, instead passing over it with a cross-reference to other Vinaya ordinances [Hüsken 1997].
